name: What should I do first before removing an interior wall?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first before removing an interior wall?

acceptedAnswer.text:
First, stop demolition and determine whether the wall supports framing, a roof, another floor, or concentrated loads. A qualified remodeling team should inspect the wall, attic or crawlspace, and nearby utilities before recommending removal.

Context: A wall that looks like a simple divider may carry vertical loads or conceal electrical, plumbing, HVAC, or gas lines. Removing it can require temporary support, engineered framing, plan review, and finish repairs.

Key factors:
- Wall direction and framing alignment
- Stories, roof loads, and beams above
- Utility locations and outlet circuits
- Existing plans, prior remodels, and foundation conditions

Practical guidance: Photograph both sides, the ceiling, attic access, and any visible vents or plumbing before requesting an evaluation. Elite Remodeling & Design can review the desired layout as part of a coordinated design and construction plan.

A careful assessment before demolition is usually the fastest way to avoid structural and utility surprises.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stop before opening or removing the wall. Have its structural role and hidden electrical, plumbing, HVAC, or gas services checked first; then determine whether temporary support, engineering, permits, and finish repairs are needed.
